verdict.rationale: Clerk's eve tool-call authorization guide says it can broker OAuth for tools that need a provider token on the caller's behalf, which is the core of delegated third-party access for agent tool calls. The evidence is a single summary line, with no detail on token lifetime, consent flow, storage or exchange mechanics. Missing for 10: documented short-lived token issuance and expiry, explicit user-consent flow details, token vault storage and refresh mechanics, supported third-party providers, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent obtain short-lived, user-consented tokens for third-party APIs (token vault/exchange) so tool calls run under the user's delegated authority

citations.quote: broker OAuth for tools that need a provider token on the caller's behalf
